questionsToConsider: Which services do you actually offer, and should any of them lead to their own follow-up questions?
Do you take emergency work, and who is on call to phone those customers back?
Which details change your price, such as area size, number of units or access at height?
Do business customers need a purchase order before you can invoice them?
Should customers upload photos, and will someone look at them before the visit?
guide.howToUseResponses: Sort new orders by urgency first: emergencies need a phone call, not an email. For planned work, check the description and photos to decide who to send and what to bring, then reply with a confirmed date and price so the customer knows the order is accepted. Keep the purchase order number with the job so the invoice matches what the business expects.
customizeSteps: Replace the list of services with the work you do, and add a short description where two options could be confused.
Rewrite the emergency ending with the real response you can promise, or remove the emergency option if you don't offer one.
Share the link from your website's booking page or embed the form there, then test both the home and business paths.

faqs.q: What should a service order form include?
faqs.a: Who the customer is, what work they need, where it will happen, when they want it done and anything that affects access. Photos and a purchase order number help when you need to quote or invoice a business.

faqs.q: What's the difference between a service order and a service request?
faqs.a: A request asks whether you can help. An order describes specific work the customer wants done, which you then confirm with a date and price.

faqs.q: Does a submitted order mean the job is booked?
faqs.a: Not in this template. The ending tells customers you'll confirm the date and price, so nobody assumes a slot is held before you've checked.

faqs.q: Can I take orders for more than one type of service?
faqs.a: Yes. The service question lists each kind of work, and you can add a branch so one of them, such as installations, gets its own follow-up questions.

doc.title: Service order
doc.description: Collect the job, the site and the timing so your team can plan the visit.

blocks.title: Hi there. Tell us about the job and we'll get it planned.
First, who should we contact about this order?
Is this for your home or for a business?
Do you have a purchase order number or quote reference?
blocks.description: Leave it blank if you don't have one yet.

blocks.title: What kind of work do you need?
Describe the job in a few sentences.
blocks.description: What's wrong or what you want done, the make or model if there is one, and roughly how big the area is.

blocks.title: Where will the work take place?
Anything we should know about getting in and working on site?
blocks.description: Parking, gate codes, key collection, pets, or rooms we shouldn't enter.

blocks.title: Got photos of the problem or the space? Add up to five.
How soon do you need us?
Is anything unsafe right now, such as a gas smell, flooding or exposed wiring?
blocks.description: If so, keep everyone clear and call your local emergency number before anything else.

blocks.title: Which date would suit you best?
blocks.description: We'll confirm the actual date once we've checked the schedule.

blocks.title: Which times work for a visit?

endings.title: Order received ✅
endings.bodyMd: We'll check the details and send you a confirmed date and price. Nothing is booked until you hear back from us.

endings.title: We're on it
endings.bodyMd: Emergency orders go straight to the on-call team, and someone will phone you shortly on the number you gave us.

closeRules.closedMessageMd: This form is no longer accepting responses.

requireAuth.message: Before we start, could you verify who you are? It only takes a moment.
